message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Welcome to Aurex’s ranks. You will learn to read cards, deploy units, overcome DEF, use an active ability, and play a tactic.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Each card shows its ENE cost, name, type, and statistics. HP is the damage a unit can endure; DEF is protection that must be removed; ATK is base-attack strength. The Tribune costs 2 ENE and also has an ability.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Collapse the Hand for a clearer view of the map.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Reopen the Hand. You can collapse and show it whenever needed.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Select The Tribune. After choosing a unit card, the map highlights legal deployment cells.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Deploy The Tribune on the indicated cell. Units without Vanguard enter exhausted and can act on a later turn.

deploy-tribune.wrongActionText: Deploy The Tribune on the highlighted cell.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: A Nexus Robot Trooper enters the training area. It has 2 HP, 1 DEF, and 2 ATK.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: A normal attack hits DEF first. While the target has DEF, excess strength does not pass to HP. After DEF reaches zero, a later attack can damage HP.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: The Tribune is exhausted. End the turn so it will be ready on the next one.

end-first-turn.wrongActionText: End the turn with the highlighted button.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: The Nexus holds position. It is your turn again: deploy the Heavy Legionary before committing the Tribune.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Select the Heavy Legionary. It costs 3 ENE and has 3 HP, 2 DEF, and 4 ATK.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Deploy the Legionary on the indicated cell. It enters exhausted but will be ready after the Nexus turn.

deploy-legionary.wrongActionText: Deploy the Legionary on the highlighted cell.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Select The Tribune. It is ready and adjacent to the Robot Trooper.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Attack the Robot Trooper. The Tribune’s 2 ATK will remove its only DEF; excess damage will not reach HP yet.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: The Robot Trooper’s DEF is now zero. After the Nexus turn, the Legionary is ready to use Heavy Blow.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Select the Heavy Legionary.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Press the ability button. Heavy Blow costs 1 ENE, deals 2 damage within range 2, and then enters cooldown.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Strike the Robot Trooper. With no DEF, 2 damage will directly remove its 2 HP.

heavy-blow-target.wrongActionText: Use Heavy Blow on the Robot Trooper.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: The Nexus responds with a Heavy Mech: 4 HP, 3 DEF, and 3 ATK. One action will not be enough; coordinate tactic and units.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: EMP Missile is a tactic. It costs 3 ENE, deals 2 damage, and permanently reduces the target’s ATK by 1. Tactics do not become miniatures: they resolve from the Hand.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Select EMP Missile.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Launch EMP Missile at the Heavy Mech.

emp-target-mech.wrongActionText: Target the Heavy Mech with EMP Missile.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: The Missile removed 2 DEF, leaving the Mech with 1. Its ATK also fell from 3 to 2. The Tribune can now break the last protection.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Select The Tribune.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Attack the Heavy Mech. The Tribune will remove its last DEF, setting up the decisive blow.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: The Mech retaliates against the Legionary. EMP reduces its attack to 2: it removes DEF but does not reach HP. The Mech now has no protection.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Select the Heavy Legionary for the final blow.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Attack. With DEF at zero, the Legionary’s 4 ATK will hit the Mech’s 4 HP and destroy it.

destroy-mech.wrongActionText: Attack the Heavy Mech with the Legionary.

message.speaker: Exordium Narrator
message.text: Lesson complete. You read and played unit cards, removed DEF before HP, used an active ability, and coordinated EMP Missile with two attacks.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Welcome to the Nexus network. This lesson covers the Starter reserve, the differences between Infantry, Vehicles, and Structures, and the advantage of Vanguard.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: The three Starter cards always remain in reserve: one Infantry, one Vehicle, and one Structure. They are neither drawn nor consumed when used; you still pay their ENE cost and obey battlefield limits.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: The Security Droid is the Starter Infantry. Infantry moves one cell and can still attack, use an ability, or build a Structure after moving.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Select the Security Droid from the Starter reserve.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Deploy the Droid on the indicated cell near the HQ. Like almost every newly deployed unit, it enters exhausted.

deploy-security-droid.wrongActionText: Deploy the Droid on the highlighted cell.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: The Starter card remains in reserve. You may deploy more copies while ENE, space, and mode limits allow it.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: End the turn. The Droid will be ready when the network returns to your control.

end-turn-for-infantry.wrongActionText: End the turn with the highlighted button.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: The turn returns to the Nexus. The Droid can now move and then build during the same turn.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Select the Security Droid. Reachable cells will be highlighted immediately.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Move the Droid to the indicated cell. It will remain ready to build after moving.

move-security-droid.wrongActionText: Move the Droid to the highlighted cell.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: The Armed Barrier is the Starter Structure. Structures cannot move but become new network nodes: units may deploy on the HQ or open cells adjacent to an allied building.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Select the Armed Barrier from the Starter reserve. The Droid that just moved will act as builder.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Build the Barrier on the indicated cell. The Infantry moved and now uses its action to extend the deployment network.

build-forward-structure.wrongActionText: Build the Barrier on the highlighted cell.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: The forward node is operational. This Structure lets you deploy new units closer to the central Strategic Point.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: The turn returns to the Nexus. The Scout Quad is the Starter Vehicle: at Fast pace it can move up to two cells, but normally must choose between movement and an action.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Select the Scout Quad from the Starter reserve.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Deploy the Quad on the indicated cell made available by the forward Barrier.

deploy-quad-from-network.wrongActionText: Deploy the Quad on the highlighted cell.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: The Quad reached the center but enters exhausted. An ordinary Vehicle must wait until the next turn before moving.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: End the turn to ready the Quad.

end-turn-for-quad.wrongActionText: End the turn with the highlighted button.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: The Quad is ready. It will now complete the ordinary route to the Strategic Point.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Select the Scout Quad. Reachable cells will be highlighted immediately.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Move the Quad onto the central Strategic Point.

quad-captures-center.wrongActionText: Move the Quad onto the central Strategic Point.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: First procedure complete: forward network, Vehicle deployment, one waiting turn, and movement onto the Strategic Point.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: The Quad clears the center for comparison. The Light Mech is a Hand card with Vanguard, so it can act on the turn it enters play.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Select the Light Mech from the Hand.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Deploy the Mech on the same cell of the forward network. Vanguard will keep it ready.

deploy-vanguard-from-network.wrongActionText: Deploy the Mech on the highlighted cell.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: The Mech is not exhausted. Select it: reachable cells will be highlighted and it can move immediately.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Move the Mech onto the Strategic Point. Vanguard removed the waiting turn.

vanguard-captures-center.wrongActionText: Move the Mech onto the central Strategic Point.

message.speaker: Nexus Narrator
message.text: Lesson complete. You used the Starter reserve, moved and built with Infantry, extended the network with a Structure, reached the center with a Vehicle, and compared ordinary deployment with Vanguard.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: The Agathoi line does not win by chasing every target. You will learn to choose the right defense, hold a Strategic Point, and withstand three Exordium waves.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: The Border Hoplite guards the central Point with 3 HP, 3 DEF, and permanent Thorns 1. The adjacent Healing Grove keeps the allied network open for defensive tactics.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: Your Hand offers several answers, but the first wave is fragile. Thorn Cloak raises Thorns to 2 until the next turn, the most efficient choice against a light assault.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: Select Thorn Cloak.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: Apply Thorn Cloak to the Hoplite.

apply-thorns-to-oplite.wrongActionText: Target the Border Hoplite with Thorn Cloak.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: The Hoplite now deals 2 direct damage to attackers. Thorns do not prevent an enemy strike, but make every assault costly.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: End the turn and let the Exordium strike the line.

end-turn-wave-one.wrongActionText: End the turn with the highlighted button.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: The Guard removed part of the Hoplite’s DEF, but Thorns 2 destroyed it. The first wave was repelled without spending an attack.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: The second wave is tougher. Vigilant Nature grants Counterattack: if the Hoplite survives a base attack, it immediately retaliates once.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: Select Vigilant Nature.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: Grant Counterattack to the Hoplite.

apply-counterattack-to-oplite.wrongActionText: Target the Border Hoplite with Vigilant Nature.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: Thorns and Counterattack are different reactions. Thorns deal direct damage; Counterattack uses the Hoplite’s ATK and hits enemy DEF first.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: End the turn and prepare the Hoplite’s response.

end-turn-wave-two.wrongActionText: End the turn with the highlighted button.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: The Legionary broke the Hoplite’s last DEF. Thorns wounded it and Counterattack destroyed it. The Hoplite retains all its HP.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: The third wave targets the Grove. Wooden Bastion sets the Structure’s current DEF equal to its HP, the right choice against one powerful strike.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: Select Wooden Bastion.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: Fortify the Healing Grove.

fortify-healing-grove.wrongActionText: Target the Healing Grove with Wooden Bastion.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: The Grove now has 4 DEF, equal to its 4 HP. As long as a strike meets at least one DEF, excess damage does not pass through the protection.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: End the turn. The last wave will try to demolish the Structure.

end-turn-wave-three.wrongActionText: End the turn with the highlighted button.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: The Artillery removed all DEF but dealt no HP damage to the Grove. The fortification absorbed the blow and the line can respond.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: Select the Hoplite. It survived the waves and is still ready to act.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: Attack the Artillery. With no DEF and 2 HP remaining, the Hoplite’s 2 ATK will destroy it.

destroy-third-wave.wrongActionText: Attack the Exordium Artillery with the Hoplite.

message.speaker: Agathoi Narrator
message.text: Lesson complete. You chose three different defenses, turned enemy attacks into damage with Thorns and Counterattack, fortified a Structure, and held the Point.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: The Agathoi hold the central Point with a Stone Anthropos. One blow will not defeat it: read your Hand, choose the right cards, and turn numbers into pressure.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: The Anthropos has 6 HP and 4 DEF. Three Liberti Infantry surround it: when at least one ally is adjacent to the same target, Numerical Superiority adds +1 ATK to the attack.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: Hover over the cards and read their previews. During the tutorial, previews remain fully visible even while the rest of the screen is dimmed. Find a card that applies Bleeding 2 to an Infantry unit’s next attack.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: Choose the Hand card that prepares Bleeding 2 on an Infantry unit’s next base attack.

choose-sanguis-card.wrongActionText: Compare the effects: you need Mark of the Sanguis.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: Apply Mark of the Sanguis to the highlighted Militiaman.

apply-sanguis-mark.wrongActionText: Target the highlighted Militiaman with Mark of the Sanguis.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: Select the Marked Militiaman.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: Attack the Anthropos. Numerical Superiority raises the Militiaman from 2 to 3 ATK: it will remove 3 of 4 DEF and apply Bleeding 2.

superiority-attack.wrongActionText: Attack the Stone Anthropos with the selected Militiaman.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: DEF fell from 4 to 1. The target still has 6 HP, but Bleeding 2 will strike directly at the start of its turn, ignoring remaining DEF.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: End the turn to trigger Bleeding.

end-turn-for-bleed.wrongActionText: End the turn with the highlighted button.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: Bleeding directly removed 2 HP: the Anthropos fell to 4 HP while retaining 1 DEF. Now use a card that turns the encirclement into immediate attacks.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: Choose the card that orders Infantry adjacent to the enemy to attack immediately, even if they have already acted.

choose-coordinated-card.wrongActionText: You need a coordinated-attack card: Attack Lure.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: Play Attack Lure on the surrounded Anthropos.

play-coordinated-attack.wrongActionText: Target the Stone Anthropos with Attack Lure.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: Attack Lure activated the Infantry in sequence. The first removed the last DEF; the others depleted the HP. The central Point is now clear.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: Select the Liberti Raider. The coordinated reactions did not consume its normal action.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: Move the Raider onto the Strategic Point and complete the assault.

capture-center-ps.wrongActionText: Move the Raider onto the central Strategic Point.

message.speaker: Liberti Narrator
message.text: Lesson complete. You compared cards through previews, chose the right answer, applied Bleeding, used Numerical Superiority, and turned encirclement into conquest.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: The Nexus left a Robot Trooper isolated. Do not destroy it: first make it vulnerable, then use the Mark to transfer control to the Citadel.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Purple Sentence costs 2 ENE. The Marked target takes +1 damage from attacks and offensive abilities until end of turn; that Mark also satisfies a Fabeot acquisition clause.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Select the Fabeot Hierarch.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Activate Purple Sentence.

activate-purple-sentence.wrongActionText: Activate Purple Sentence from the unit panel.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Apply the Mark to the Robot Trooper.

mark-fante-with-vulnerability.wrongActionText: Target the Robot Trooper with Purple Sentence.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: The Robot Trooper is Marked and Vulnerable: the next attack gains +1 damage. Its DEF will be removed while its 2 HP remain within Acquisition Clause’s limit.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Select the Fabeot Adept.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Attack the Robot Trooper. The Adept has 1 ATK, but Vulnerability adds 1 damage and removes its only DEF without damaging HP.

exploit-fabeot-vulnerability.wrongActionText: Attack the Robot Trooper with the selected Adept.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: The target is still alive, costs 2, has 2 HP, and retains the Mark. Every condition of Acquisition Clause is now visible on the map.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Select the Fabeot Citadel.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Activate Acquisition Clause. It costs 4 ENE and converts an eligible target that is already Marked.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Convert the Marked Robot Trooper.

convert-marked-fante.wrongActionText: Use the Clause on the Marked Robot Trooper.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: The Robot Trooper is now under Fabeot control. It enters exhausted and Action-Inhibited: conversion is permanent but grants no immediate action.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Now control the opponent’s resources. Embargo blocks one card per Fabeot Strategic Point; Usury Contract removes 1 ENE and reduces income by 1 for two turns.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Play Embargo. The Outpost controls a Strategic Point and the Nexus Hand contains one card, so the outcome is deterministic.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Embargo blocked the Nexus’s only card for one turn. The number of affected cards comes from controlled Strategic Points, not a hidden choice.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Play Usury Contract to disrupt the Nexus reservoir and its next ENE income.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: The Nexus reservoir fell from 5 to 4 ENE and will suffer -1 ENE on its next two income steps. Hand, territory, and resources are three distinct levers of Fabeot control.

message.speaker: Fabeot Narrator
message.text: Lesson complete. You applied a Vulnerability Mark, prepared and converted the target, blocked the enemy Hand, and disrupted ENE flow without relying on chance.

lesson-welcome.text: Welcome to Aurex’s ranks. The Nexus prefers to measure the field until the moment has passed; we learn to read it and strike when it matters. Cards, deployment, DEF, abilities, and tactics are parts of the same assault.

explain-defense.text: A normal attack removes DEF first. Excess ATK does not pass to HP: spending 4 ATK on the last DEF wastes strength you could save for the next strike. Open the protection with the right blow, then hit HP.

mech-arrival.text: The Nexus responds with a Heavy Mech: 4 HP, 3 DEF, and 3 ATK. Do not spread your fire: an enemy left alive keeps acting. Focus your tactic and several units on one target until it is destroyed.

tribune-breaks-mech-defense.text: Use The Tribune to remove the last DEF. It is the least expensive blow that opens the HP: save the Legionary’s ATK for the exposed target.

destroy-mech.text: Now the Legionary ends the assault. With DEF at zero, its 4 ATK hits 4 HP: this is where heavy power pays off, not one strike earlier.

lesson-complete.text: Lesson complete. A serious assault begins when the ENE reservoir, available tactics, and ability cooldowns align. Against Nexus calculations or Fabeot contracts, a half-attack gives them the turn they were waiting for.

nexus-welcome.text: Training protocol active. Objective: turn HQ, Infantry, Structures, and Vanguard into a network of presence and deployment. Evaluate every position by cost, coverage, and operational continuity.

read-starter-structure.text: The Armed Barrier is the Starter Structure. A Structure can occupy an SP like any other field unit; if built on a legally accessible SP, it maintains control while creating a deployment node.

build-forward-structure.text: Build the Barrier on the indicated cell. Infantry converts movement into infrastructure: the new position does more than defend—it shortens future deployments.

deployment-network-online.text: The forward node is operational immediately. If you still have ENE, a unit card, and legal space, use the newly built Structure to deploy an advanced unit closer to the front during the same turn.

vanguard-captures-center.text: Move the Mech onto the Strategic Point. Control matters only if the network can sustain it: occupying an SP you cannot reinforce turns a temporary advantage into lost ENE and time.

nexus-lesson-complete.text: Lesson complete. Operating rule: build where the network shortens reinforcement routes, and take an SP when its expected holding cost is lower than the value it produces.

agathoi-welcome.text: The Agathoi line does not win by chasing every target. The Liberti call it momentum when it often leaves important ground exposed. Here you will choose what must stand and make every attempt to take it costly.

defensive-line-overview.text: The Border Hoplite guards the central Point with 3 HP, 3 DEF, and permanent Thorns 1. A well-defended SP is not necessarily the one with the most units; it is the one whose fall would truly break your position.

wave-two-resolved.text: The Legionary broke the Hoplite’s last DEF, but Thorns and Counterattack destroyed it. Preserving advantage means reaching the next turn with the SP, HP, and another response still available.

choose-fortification.text: The third wave targets the Grove. Wooden Bastion raises the Structure’s current DEF to its HP. Do not fortify everything: invest where a loss would open the SP or the network supporting the rest of the line.

agathoi-lesson-complete.text: Lesson complete. You cannot defend every SP equally. Choose those you can sustain, protect those holding the position together, and make the opponent pay to attack where you are ready.

liberti-welcome.text: The Agathoi walled off the center with a Stone Anthropos. The Nexus build cages and the Fabeot contracts; neither likes it when the front changes direction. Turn numbers and movement into a breach instead of charging the hardest point.

liberti-formation-overview.text: The Anthropos has 6 HP and 4 DEF. Three Liberti Infantry surround it: Numerical Superiority adds +1 ATK when an ally shares the target. Liberti strength is landing several attacks on one enemy before it can recover.

coordinated-pressure-resolved.text: Attack Lure activated the Infantry in sequence: the first removed the last DEF and the others depleted HP. That is the value of focused attacks: one sequence finishes the job instead of leaving several enemies half damaged.

capture-center-ps.text: Move the Raider onto the Strategic Point. Removing the guard is not enough: the assault creates advantage only when you reoccupy the Point and force the opponent to react to your position.

liberti-lesson-complete.text: Lesson complete. When behind, do not chase the best-defended SP: strike an exposed one, force the enemy to move, and reopen the front. SPs are levers; use the one that yields.

fabeot-welcome.text: The Nexus left a Robot Trooper isolated. Predictable. Others call property what they have not yet lost: first make the target vulnerable, then transfer control to the Citadel.

fabeot-contract-overview.text: Purple Sentence costs 2 ENE. The Mark adds 1 offensive damage and satisfies an acquisition clause. An effect matters only when it opens the next: Mark, damage, and acquisition are worth more than their sum in the correct order.

fabeot-embargo-resolved.text: Embargo blocked the Nexus’s only card for one turn. Each controlled SP increases how many cards you can block. Territory is not scenery; it is capital converted into pressure on the enemy Hand.

fabeot-usury-resolved.text: The Nexus reservoir fell from 5 to 4 ENE and will suffer -1 on its next two income steps. Anyone who attacks without considering ENE, cooldowns, and available tactics treats resources as carelessly as everyone else. We prefer the opponent to do that.

fabeot-lesson-complete.text: Lesson complete. The game engine turns on SPs: ENE, Pressure, and deployment positions force everyone to choose. If one SP is too protected, threaten another; when the defense moves, value changes hands.
